headline: Houthi attack sparks fire at Saudi Aramco facility, Riyadh rattled by explosions
summary: Houthi strikes hit an Aramco operations center, causing explosions in Riyadh and wounding four people. The escalation follows a recent attack on Riyadh's international airport.
details: Powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital yesterday, hours after a Houthi strike hit a building housing energy giant Aramco’s operations centre. The civil defence agency reported that four people—two women, a man, and a child—were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles, and 15 homes were damaged.

In response, the Saudi-led coalition struck oil sites across western Yemen. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki stated these attacks targeted facilities used to supply the Houthis’ efforts to threaten the kingdom and Red Sea waterways.

The Houthis claimed responsibility, stating they targeted Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport, and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh. Following these events, international benchmark Brent crude futures rose by 0.3% to $105.97 per barrel.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) reportedly denied a request from Israel to join the fight against the Houthis in Yemen. A diplomatic source indicated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had offered assistance via US mediation, partly to strengthen ties with the kingdom.

MBS opposed the move, fearing a backlash among the Saudi public. The Saudi-led coalition has militarily supported Yemen’s government against the Houthis since 2015, a conflict that has led to a severe humanitarian crisis. Civilians in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital were seen queuing for fuel, fearing shortages.

This surge in violence follows a strike on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, which resulted in 13 deaths and suspended operations, marking the worst attack on the kingdom since 2015. The Saudi cabinet, led by MBS, vowed not to allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait to be threatened.

Several countries have issued travel warnings for their citizens in Saudi Arabia. France, for instance, advised its nationals on Tuesday to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam airports due to the heightened security situation.
